title: The Cell System: a coordinate system for the odd sieve — what it proves, what it measures, and where it stops
description:
Twelve papers, one overview and thirty-three verification scripts on the elementary sieve of the odd numbers, developed as a coordinate system of lines and cells.

Papers 1 to 4 build the coordinates and the transport laws: an exact histogram for the increments of floor(2j²/n) with no error term, the line/cell coordinate system, the exact inheritance law on a full sieve cycle, and what survives when that law is evaluated on a short interval. Papers 5 to 8 are the construction and what it decides about twin pairs: the three-letter gap alphabet, the six exception positions of the twin criterion, clocks and the capacity of a single line, and the belts between consecutive prime squares. Papers 9 to 11 derive the point at which the construction stops, from inside it rather than by quoting it: the depth cut, the unique-owner theorem, the exact twin count T = C − R + S with no error term and the parity identity 2(R − C) = Σ(−1)Ω, both under the cut that the section states; then why no ordinary sieve crosses it; then four tests of the framework against problems whose answers are known independently; and finally what an external ingredient would have to supply, with every route already tried recorded, each at the width its own measurement supports. Paper 12 stands apart from the system and uses none of its objects.

The framework reproduces Buchstab's decomposition and the Hardy–Littlewood singular series without importing them, and reaches the linear-sieve identity I(s) = 2f1(s) — an identity between the two sieve functions, whose application to counting pairs would need a sequence, a density and a level of distribution that are not supplied here. It then halts exactly where the field halts. (The sifting limits are quoted from the literature, not derived here.) Paper 1 is independent of the rest and concerns no prime numbers.

Statements that are only measured are labelled as such and listed together; results produced and then retracted during the work are kept rather than deleted. No progress toward the twin-prime conjecture is claimed, and no new bound. Priority is not claimed for any result.

Release 1.1.0. Two papers are corrected and three verification scripts are added; no measured number changes. Paper 9. The pair-overlap bound is given in its sharpened form: the complete region of admissible coefficients, whose two extreme points are the published bound and, at the cubic cut, the exact identity T = C − R + S — so the bound and the identity were one family seen from opposite ends, and the published branch loses eight ninths of the gap there. The ratio R/C and the threshold 0.5385 are relabelled as predictions of a stated model rather than limits, both being derived for rough numbers counted singly while R and C carry a partner-survival condition; the reading is cross-referenced to where it is measured. The linear-sieve identity I(s) = 2f1(s) is separated from any statement about counting pairs, which would need a sequence, a density and a level of distribution the paper does not supply. The quantity A is re-described: it counts pairs of begun lines landing on one endpoint, it is identically zero at the cut, and every contribution to it comes from endpoints with three prime factors rather than from semiprimes in a short interval. Three negative conclusions — on the partner condition, on Elliott–Halberstam, and on the greedy-covering control — are narrowed to what their measurements support. Paper 6. The claim that the maximal strike multiplicity has the order of its mean is withdrawn: a maximum over the cells is not controlled by their average, and the order is proved to be Θ(log M / log log M), with an explicit witness and with the exact Bonferroni remainder at every odd truncation, which makes the termination criterion necessary as well as sufficient. The accessible range is shown not to separate the two candidate orders, so the correction rests on the construction and not on the table. Corollary 1e is strengthened to O(X/log³X) by a published polynomial sieve bound. The root-pair hypothesis is restored to the abstract and to the summary, with the sector M = 9 recorded as the counterexample that requires it. The Fejér discrepancy proof is completed for the absolute value it states, and the sieve exponent of its appendix is corrected. A script withdrawn in an earlier pass but still present in the tree is removed. Overview and Paper 11. The same narrowings are carried into the summary entries that restate them: the multiplicity order, the two extreme points of the coefficient region, the model status of 0.5385, the reading of I(s) = 2f1(s), the rate now available for the exception count, and the scope of the greedy-covering control, which is stated with the three things it does not settle. A housekeeping pass over the whole set corrects the citation note carried by most of the set, which still described it as an eleven-part set and cited the range as [P1] to [P11] after the twelfth part was added, and the site's publication date and one paper's subtitle.
